verdict_reason: ANSWERING THE QUESTION PUT TO ME: yes, the correlation family alone is the right thing to keep, and I proved it rather than asserting it. On a 10-case synthetic panel (N=4000, D=256) the CORRELATION family recovers the planted spike fraction EXACTLY in 10 of 10 cases -- 0.0000 on all four nulls (iid isotropic; lognormal per-dimension variances at sd_log 1.0 and 1.5; one rogue dimension at variance 1e6) and exactly 1/256, 3/256, 5/256 and 20/256 when 1, 3, 5 and 20 shared directions are planted, INCLUDING 5/256 when a rogue 1e6 dimension or lognormal heteroscedasticity is added on top. The two demoted families fail that panel: `*_cov` reads outlier_frac 0.3984-0.4453 and spike_energy 0.9565-0.9975 on data with ZERO shared structure, and `perm_*` false-positives on the pure iid null (1/256, spike_energy 0.0062) and collapses to 1/256 with perm_top_ratio 1.000 when one rogue dimension is added to five genuine spikes. The routing is correct in practice: on gpt2, distilgpt2 and pythia-70m the unprefixed `mp_` keys are exactly the correlation family and every `*_cov` and `perm_*` key lands under `_meta_mp_`. The underlying RMT machinery was verified last round (_mp_cdf vs scipy.integrate.quad to max 9.5e-8 across gamma in [0.05, 4.0], correct 1-1/gamma atom, sigma^2 recovery within 0.4% for gamma <= 1.29) and nothing in this change touches it.
comparable_reason: Unchanged and re-confirmed locally. The entire cross-model spread of the promoted keys is smaller than their within-model layer spread: over gpt2 / distilgpt2 / pythia-70m, mp_ks_distance_mean = 0.6032 / 0.6222 / 0.6377 (range 0.0345), mp_outlier_frac_mean = 0.1441 / 0.1411 / 0.1387 (range 0.0054) and mp_spike_energy_mean = 0.6063 / 0.6246 / 0.5867 (range 0.0379), while ks_distance alone moves 0.5851-0.7170 across layers within these same three models. The prior 6-model sweep put mp_ks_distance_mean and mp_lower_outlier_frac_mean at Spearman -0.94 to -0.97 against d_model / n_layers / n_params over exactly that kind of range. The fixed-gamma family that exists to fix this still needs ceil(D/0.25) = 4*d_model tokens against a measured corpus of ~12,894 tokens (gamma_first = 0.05956 at D=768), so every model with d_model > ~3220 gets NaN for all six *_g25 keys.
github_repo: no code accompanies Marchenko & Pastur (1967) or Baik-Ben Arous-Peche (2005); cross-checked against an independent scipy.integrate.quad implementation of the MP density
github_reason: The cited sources are 1967 and 2005 theory papers with no released code, so 'the original code' is legitimately NONE. The reference was built instead: scipy quad on sqrt((t+ - t)(t - t-))/(2 pi gamma t) plus the exact atom 1 - 1/gamma for gamma > 1, on a 25-point grid at ten aspect ratios; max absolute deviation from _mp_cdf 2.4e-8 to 9.5e-8. This round the check that mattered was behavioural rather than formulaic -- the 10-case planted-spike panel above, where the correlation family's answer is exact in every case.
paper_reason: Marchenko-Pastur publishes a limiting law and BBP a phase-transition threshold; neither contains a figure or table this implementation could reproduce for transformer activations, and Staats et al. (2024), cited for the lower-edge statistic, reports deviations for their own trained networks on their own data. The reproducible analytic anchors are the ones tested: the bulk edges (1 +/- sqrt(gamma))^2, the atom mass 1 - 1/gamma, the MP CDF to 9.5e-8, and -- new this round -- exact recovery of k/D for k = 1, 3, 5, 20 planted directions in D = 256.
confounds_reason: Standing: five of the promoted summary keys were monotone in scale at |rho| >= 0.77 over six models, with mp_ks_distance_mean and mp_lower_outlier_frac_mean at -0.94 to -0.97, over total ranges of 0.035-0.054 that I reproduced locally (0.0054-0.0379 over three models). The MP null is gamma-matched, so the gamma = D/N channel enters through the aspect ratio rather than through d_model directly, but the *_g25 family that would break that link is NaN for exactly the wide models where it matters. The demotion of the *_cov and perm_* families removes two of the worst offenders from the feature matrix -- perm_outlier_frac sat at the 1/D floor in 7 of 9 real layers -- so the confound is narrower than it was, not gone.
defects: mp_edge_tol = 0.05 is STILL written into the results dict without a _meta_ prefix (rmt_bulk.py, last line of evaluate). Confirmed present in all three real runs. It is a configuration constant, so it enters the analysis feature matrix as a zero-variance column. Flagged in the previous two rounds and unfixed; it is a one-word change.

mp_lower_outlier_frac is very nearly a duplicate of mp_ks_distance and BOTH are in the feature matrix. Measured over the 9 real per-layer values (3 models x first/mid/last): Pearson 0.9968, Spearman 1.0, mean |difference| 0.0194 -- 0.6168 vs 0.6016, 0.6079 vs 0.5846, 0.5851 vs 0.5651, 0.6345 vs 0.6211, 0.6281 vs 0.6055, 0.6040 vs 0.5833, 0.5897 vs 0.5703, 0.6064 vs 0.5840, 0.7170 vs 0.6992. mp_lower_energy is genuinely independent (Pearson with ks 0.133) and worth keeping; lower_outlier_frac is not.

The perm_* family is still COMPUTED at full cost -- 12 D x D permutations and eigendecompositions per layer -- and then routed to _meta_, where by the code's own docstring nothing should read it. Measured wall time for the whole task on this host: 92.7 s (gpt2), 62.4 s (distilgpt2), 73.0 s (pythia-70m), the bulk of which is that null. If the family is not trustworthy enough to be a feature, it does not need to be recomputed on every run; gate it behind a config flag.

The demoted keys keep the misleading NAME. `_meta_mp_spike_energy_cov` still says 'spike' while reading 0.9767 (gpt2), 0.9768 (distilgpt2) and 0.8517 (pythia-70m) -- values I showed reach 0.9565-0.9975 on synthetic data with no shared structure at all. Demotion keeps it out of regressions but not out of an audit reader's eye; mp_isotropy_dev_energy_cov would be the honest name.

The module docstring's Method section still says 'ratio gamma = D/N' while _mp_metrics_core computes gamma = D/max(1, n_tokens - 1). Numerically immaterial (measured indistinguishable in sigma^2 recovery down to gamma = 1.3) but the docstring is wrong, and this was raised last round.

The Metrics section of the module docstring still describes mp_spike_energy as 'the fraction of total variance carried by structured (BBP supercritical) spikes' with no mention that this holds for the CORRELATION variant only, nor of the newly emitted lower_* and _meta_ families. The emitted key set has roughly quadrupled and the docstring lists three keys.

The *_g25 family still becomes NaN for exactly the wide models where a fixed aspect ratio would matter: it needs 4*d_model tokens and the shipped corpus yields ~12,894 (measured from gamma_first = 0.05956 at D = 768), so the cutoff is d_model ~ 3220.

The correlation family's blindness to rogue dimensions is now the intended scope rather than a bug, but nothing in the EMITTED keys says so -- a reader of mp_spike_energy has no signal that a massive-activation dimension is invisible to it by construction. The demoted *_cov keys are the only record and they are the ones a reader is told to ignore.
fix: The routing decision is correct -- keep the correlation family and only the correlation family in the feature matrix; my planted-spike panel is unambiguous (exact k/D recovery in 10 of 10 cases, exact 0.0000 on four different nulls).
